# core/tls13.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/tls13.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

The key schedule of TLS 1.3 with SHA-256 (RFC 8446
section 7): HKDF-Expand-Label, Derive-Secret, the early, handshake and
master secrets, traffic keys and IVs, record nonces and Finished values.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and each
function returns the number of bytes its name says (32 for a secret, 12
for an IV or a nonce, the asked-for length for a key). Not proved: that
the values are the standard's; the tests check the values of RFC 8448
(the early secret, `derived`, the handshake secret) and values computed
by a Python reference for the rest.

`import "core/tls13.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/sha256.bastio](core-sha256.md), [core/hkdf.bastio](core-hkdf.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`tls13_expand_label`](#tls13_expand_label) | HKDF-Expand-Label (RFC 8446 section 7.1). |
| [`tls13_derive_secret`](#tls13_derive_secret) | Derive-Secret. |
| [`tls13_early_secret`](#tls13_early_secret) | The early secret when no pre-shared key is used. |
| [`tls13_next_secret`](#tls13_next_secret) | The next secret in the schedule. |
| [`tls13_traffic_key`](#tls13_traffic_key) | The traffic key of a traffic secret. |
| [`tls13_traffic_iv`](#tls13_traffic_iv) | The IV of a traffic secret. |
| [`tls13_nonce`](#tls13_nonce) | The nonce of record number `seq`. |
| [`tls13_finished`](#tls13_finished) | The Finished message's verify data. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `tls13_expand_label`

```bastio
fn tls13_expand_label(secret: &Bytes, label: Str, context: &Bytes, n: u64) -> Bytes
  requires blen(secret) == 32 && slen(label) <= 249 && blen(context) <= 255 && n <= 8160
  ensures blen(result) == n
```

HKDF-Expand-Label (RFC 8446 section 7.1): `n` bytes from `secret` for the
`label` (without the "tls13 " prefix) and `context`.

Example:

```bastio
let secret = balloc(32);
let ctx = balloc(0);
let key = tls13_expand_label(secret, "key", ctx, 16);
let n = blen(key);
bfree(key);
bfree(ctx);
bfree(secret);
if n != 16 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13_derive_secret`

```bastio
fn tls13_derive_secret(secret: &Bytes, label: Str, transcript_hash: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(secret) == 32 && slen(label) <= 249 && blen(transcript_hash) <= 255
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

Derive-Secret: 32 bytes from `secret` for the `label` and the hash of the
handshake messages so far.

Example:

```bastio
let secret = balloc(32);
let hash = balloc(32);
let s = tls13_derive_secret(secret, "c hs traffic", hash);
let n = blen(s);
bfree(s);
bfree(hash);
bfree(secret);
if n != 32 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13_early_secret`

```bastio
fn tls13_early_secret() -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

The early secret when no pre-shared key is used: HKDF-Extract of 32 zero
bytes with a salt of 32 zero bytes.

Example:

```bastio
let early = tls13_early_secret();
let n = blen(early);
bfree(early);
if n != 32 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13_next_secret`

```bastio
fn tls13_next_secret(secret: &Bytes, input: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(secret) == 32
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

The next secret in the schedule: HKDF-Extract of `input` (the shared
secret of the key exchange, or 32 zero bytes for the master secret) under
the "derived" secret of `secret`.

Example:

```bastio
let early = tls13_early_secret();
let shared = balloc(32);
let hs = tls13_next_secret(early, shared);
let n = blen(hs);
bfree(hs);
bfree(shared);
bfree(early);
if n != 32 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13_traffic_key`

```bastio
fn tls13_traffic_key(secret: &Bytes, n: u64) -> Bytes
  requires blen(secret) == 32 && n <= 8160
  ensures blen(result) == n
```

The traffic key of a traffic secret: `n` bytes (16 for AES-128-GCM, 32
for ChaCha20-Poly1305).

Example:

```bastio
let secret = balloc(32);
let key = tls13_traffic_key(secret, 32);
let n = blen(key);
bfree(key);
bfree(secret);
if n != 32 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13_traffic_iv`

```bastio
fn tls13_traffic_iv(secret: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(secret) == 32
  ensures blen(result) == 12
```

The IV of a traffic secret: 12 bytes.

Example:

```bastio
let secret = balloc(32);
let iv = tls13_traffic_iv(secret);
let n = blen(iv);
bfree(iv);
bfree(secret);
if n != 12 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13_nonce`

```bastio
fn tls13_nonce(iv: &Bytes, seq: u64) -> Bytes
  requires blen(iv) == 12
  ensures blen(result) == 12
```

The nonce of record number `seq`: the IV with the sequence number, as 64
bits on the right, xored in.

Example:

```bastio
let iv = balloc(12);
let nonce = tls13_nonce(iv, 5);
let last = bget(nonce, 11);
bfree(nonce);
bfree(iv);
if last != 5 { return 1; }
```

### `tls13_finished`

```bastio
fn tls13_finished(base_secret: &Bytes, transcript_hash: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  requires blen(base_secret) == 32
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

The Finished message's verify data: HMAC-SHA-256 of the transcript hash
under the finished key of `base_secret` (a handshake traffic secret).

Example:

```bastio
let secret = balloc(32);
let hash = balloc(32);
let v = tls13_finished(secret, hash);
let n = blen(v);
bfree(v);
bfree(hash);
bfree(secret);
if n != 32 { return 1; }
```
